unobscured_target_surface_label: Example sticky-header and unobscured-target posture for official voter-information routes
delivery_role_note: Bounded unobscured-target surface for official voter-information routes that rely on fragments, jump links, or scripted scroll/reveal actions while persistent chrome remains on screen.

critical_targets.visibility_note: When the target is opened from a copied fragment or in-page navigation link, the heading and first controlling lines remain visible above the sticky site header and any active alert banner.

fragment_landing_visibility_note: Critical fragment targets land with visible heading text and operative first lines, not underneath persistent page chrome.
scripted_scroll_visibility_note: Programmatic jump or panel-open scroll behavior uses the same unobscured landing assumptions as browser-native fragment navigation.
mobile_and_zoom_offset_note: The landing review covered small-screen navigation variants and 200% zoom where the effective chrome height increases.
banner_or_alert_overlap_note: Temporary alert or maintenance banners were treated as part of the landing-visibility budget rather than ignored as a separate component concern.
collapsed_or_revealed_target_note: If the target sits inside a disclosure or accordion, the route reveals the panel and keeps the top of the answer visible above persistent chrome.
accessibility_alignment_note: Unobscured-target checks were run alongside focus/order and assistive-technology checks so the target is not merely technically focused while still visually hidden.
